France is facing a partial alcohol ban amid a historic heatwave, leaving the country’s popular music festival with no choice but to go dry.

Millions of people flock to Europe each year for Fête de la Musique, the annual French-born celebration known in English as World Music Day.

Held on the summer solstice since 1982, the festival encourages musicians of all abilities to perform in public spaces, turning entire towns and cities into open-air concert venues.

However, as temperatures climb to record-breaking levels expected to peak Monday, the French government announced a ban on public alcohol consumption in the 35 regions that are placed under its highest red heatwave alert starting at noon Sunday.

After a crisis meeting, the office of Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said in a statement: “Prefects will issue decrees banning alcohol consumption in public spaces in the departments under red alert. For all events organised by the state and its agencies, instructions have been given not to offer alcohol.”

open image in gallery The annual Fete de la Musique music festival is still continuing during a heatwave in Paris, but will no longer serve alcohol to festivalgoers ( Reuters )

Music day event organizers were ordered to limit alcohol use to “preserve emergency services and allow medics to concentrate on taking care of the most vulnerable.”

The red alert covers much of western and central France, including Paris. Many other regions are under an orange alert.

Weather service Météo-France warned that temperatures could reach as high as 41 degrees Celsius, which is around 106 degrees Fahrenheit, in some areas.

Additional safety measures were put into place ahead of Fête de la Musique celebrations. In Paris, police increased their patrols along the Seine River to prevent drownings.

French officials said that around 4,800 police officers, along with 2,500 firefighters, were deployed to maintain public safety during the celebrations.

open image in gallery World Music Day festival in France is taking place in the middle of an extreme heatwave ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery France officials announced the highest heatwave warning Sunday as temperatures reach scorching levels ( AFP via Getty Images )

The heatwave has already forced dozens of trains to be cancelled, shut down outdoor sporting events and closed 845 schools ahead of Monday. Météo-France said it is “uncertain” how long the heatwave will last.

To help Parisians and tourists stay cool during the heat, city officials are keeping parks and gardens open throughout the night in the French capital. The Eiffel Tower and other venues in Paris set up misting stations to cool crowds.

President Emmanuel Macron encouraged citizens to take care of each other amid the heatwave in a post on X, writing in French: “In the face of the heatwave, let us watch over one another. Let us collectively be attentive to our elders, to our children, and to isolated or vulnerable people.”

The Duchess of Sussex has shared a heartwarming family photograph to mark Father’s Day, featuring Prince Harry with their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.

The image, posted by Meghan on Sunday, shows a smiling Duke of Sussex kneeling and embracing Archie, who is sporting an England football top, and his daughter Lilibet.

In the Instagram post, the duchess penned a touching tribute to her husband, writing: "They’re so lucky to have you. We all are. Happy Father’s Day to our one and only." A separate message, "Happy Father’s Day" accompanied by a white heart, was shared to her stories.

The photograph captures seven-year-old Archie in a red and white England kit with dark blue shorts, while his five-year-old sister holds a soft toy giraffe. The timing of the post comes ahead of England’s next World Cup match against Ghana on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, speculation has intensified this week regarding a potential reunion between the King and his grandchildren, following reports that Harry and Meghan have been offered royal accommodation for their upcoming visit to the UK.

It has been four years since Archie and Lilibet last saw their grandfather, Charles, in person during Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee celebrations in 2022.

The Sussexes are expected to travel from their Californian residence to the UK next month. Their visit will include attending celebrations marking the one-year countdown to Harry’s Invictus Games, which will be hosted by Birmingham, alongside engagements with charities he supports, WellChild and Scotty’s Little Soldiers.

Elsewhere, the royal family marked Prince William’s 44th birthday, and Father’s Day, by releasing a previously unseen photo of him and his daughter, Princess Charlotte.

The photo, taken after this year’s Trooping the Colour, was shared on Instagram on Sunday.

It featured the caption: “Happy birthday and Father’s Day to the best Papa in the World! We love you very much. C, G, C & L” and an emoji of two pink hearts.

The picture was taken in the garden of Kensington Palace after the Trooping the Colour ceremony last weekend.

The Iranian national anthem was loudly booed again at SoFI Stadium in Los Angeles on Sunday after Iran continued their World Cup campaign against Belgium in Group G.

The reaction added to the hostile reception for the team following a similar atmosphere before they played New Zealand in a gripping 2-2 draw.

The Fifa announcer at the stadium had asked fans to “applaud for peace,” but the response was relatively muted with just a smattering of noise in support of the message.

Iran began their World cup campaign just hours after President Donald Trump announced a preliminary US-Iran peace deal had been signed to end America’s’ war with Iran.

The team flew into the US last Sunday from their training base in Tijuana, Mexico, touching down in Los Angeles just as a deal was announced to end the conflict.

Around 300 to 500 protesters ⁠gathered outside the stadium before the game, waving anti-Iranian government signs and flags. They said they did not want to attend the ​match as ⁠it would imply support for Tehran, as they protested against the country’s regime and its crackdown on pro-democracy protestors.

open image in gallery Players line up before the FIFA World Cup 2026 Group G match between Belgium and IR Iran ( Getty )

Inside, some fans then jeered Iran’s anthem as it was played ahead of their opening match.

Los Angeles is the biggest home to the Iranian community outside of Iran after many fled the country following the Islamic Revolution in 1979.

Iran's participation ⁠in the tournament has been beset by controversy against the backdrop of the war, which began in February ⁠when the US and Israel launched strikes on the country.

That followed nationwide protests in January inside Iran in which thousands were killed in a bloody government crackdown.

open image in gallery Iran played New Zealand in Los Angeles ( Getty )

In recent ‌weeks, the football team changed their ​base from Arizona to Mexico, while their federation complained that not ‌all their staff received US visas and that tickets ​allocated to supporters had been withdrawn.

A US administration official explained: “We will not allow the Iranian team to abuse this system to sneak terrorists into the United States under false pretences.”

Fifa’s ban on the pre-revolutionary Iran flag was upheld on Monday morning after an expedited hearing. The flag has the same colours as the current official flag but has a different lion-and-sun motif and is historically associated with the country’s previous Shah-led regime.

Fifa prohibits flags or apparel that have “political, offensive and/or discriminatory nature”.

Judge Curtis Kin ruled that the ban should be allowed to stand, stating: “Free speech is incredibly important, it is sacred, a bedrock of our society, but it is not without limitation, such as private actor, on private property, and as shown by previous cases, regulating in reasonable way. I deny the application.”

Two baby giraffes who went missing from a Virginia zoo last year have been found safe.

The giraffe calves vanished from the Natural Bridge Zoo in 2025 as state officials investigated allegations of animal abuse.

The Office of the Attorney General of Virginia located the giraffes, but did not share specifics about how or where they were found. The giraffes are now at a professional facility specializing in giraffe care, officials said.

Before the giraffes disappeared, state officials were looking to relocate four giraffes at the zoo after they seized about 100 animals during their investigation into the alleged abuse. At the time, two of the giraffes were pregnant and gave birth before investigators visited, but their calves were missing, WDBJ reported.

State officials said the zoo never reported the animals’ births, despite a court order requiring them to do so.

open image in gallery Two giraffe calves that vanished from a Virginia zoo last year have been found safe, officials said ( Virginia Office of the Attorney General )

Gretchen Mogensen, the co-owner of Natural Bridge Zoo, served a 100-day jail sentence after refusing to explain to the court what happened to the giraffes or to hand them over.

The two calves’ disappearance sparked a widespread search, and included radio ads including one where actress Alicia Silverstone offered $50,000 for information about the giraffes’ location.

The animals, now found safe, are receiving medical attention and behavioral support.

“This outcome reflects the Attorney General’s commitment to ensuring public safety, protecting our communities, and accountability for those who break the law. Due to the ongoing criminal investigation, no further details can be released at this time,” the attorney general’s office said.

The four co-owners of the zoo face misdemeanor charges in connection with an investigation started by the attorney general’s animal law unit in 2023.

Along with the 100 animals seized from the zoo, authorities uncovered 28 dead animals at the zoo. Authorities executed a search warrant on the zoo at the time and discovered animals living in dirty conditions without food or water.

open image in gallery The animals are now receiving medical attention ( Virginia Office of the Attorney General )

In total, 95 animals were seized from the zoo, including 16 capuchins, 14 tortoises, five lemurs and two Burmese pythons.

Other animals taken under the warrant include tamarins, gibbons, sacred ibis, ground hornbills, kookaburras, macaws, patrons, cockatoos, serval, ball pythons, red-eared slider, a turtle, a skink, donkeys, sheep, llamas and a dog.

Deborah Mogensen, Gretchen Mogensen, Karl Mogensen and Mark Easley face a combined 55 misdemeanor animal cruelty charges.

Deborah and Gretchen Mogensen and the zoo’s veterinarian, Ashley Spencer, were also charged with forgery of public records, according to the report.

News.title: Lamine Yamal transforms Spain in demolition of Saudi Arabia
News.content:
Yamal, having missed the final weeks of Barcelona’s title romp in La Liga with injury, was only given 45 minutes as he worked himself back to fitness, but in that half he showed why every left-back in the tournament will be praying they don’t have to come up against him.

By contrast, we will be watching and hoping the fun he brings does not stop. When you tune into a World Cup, you do so hoping the global talents become peacock-proud and put on a show to remind everyone why there is such chatter. How this boy, who is only just a man, obliged.

“I’ve always dreamt of being at a World Cup, and being able to score in my first match as a starter is a dream,” he gasped. “I watched the last World Cup [2022] from a classroom so being able to score here with my mum and my family in the stands is a dream come true.”

Many his age are still in classrooms, finishing their final exams before heading to university. Yamal, by contrast, is destined for the stratosphere occupied by the greats. Don’t get sucked into comparisons with those who have gone before, simply enjoy watching how his journey unfolds.

Remarkably, Yamal – who became the eighth youngest scorer in World Cup history at 18 years and 343 days – was not the youngest player to score at this tournament, that particular footnote falling to Ibrahim Mbaye, the Senegal forward from Paris St-Germain, who is 200 days his junior.

News.title: Crisis-hit England blown away inside 48 minutes ahead of Stokes return
News.content:
The Lord’s win should have changed the mood around England but now we are back in Sydney, their reputation a shambles. Rob Key, the director of cricket, faces awkward questions over the way he communicated the curfew. The Ashes was a failure of planning and professionalism and this is another example of the regime’s looseness. It is just not a professional, high-performance environment. It cannot go on if they are to be serious candidates to win back the Ashes next summer. On Key’s watch, discipline has fallen apart, the team’s public image is lower than ever and wins have dried up. This was England’s sixth loss in eight Tests and when they play a decent side such as New Zealand, they do not have the game to win consistently. Key needs a series win, badly.

Key and McCullum are two men trying to be something they are not. They do not like meetings, rules and regulations and process, but because of the Ashes hammering they were forced to take on a more serious approach. If Richard Gould and Richard Thompson, the chief executive and chair, wanted the whip to be cracked they needed to bring in new management but they blinked. Key retains their support and insiders at the England and Wales Cricket Board blame Stokes and Atkinson, but what does it say about the captain’s respect for the director of cricket and coach that he was so willing to throw the new rules in the bin? It is a sign that the Ashes scars will never heal.

Bazball stirred the nation at Trent Bridge in 2022 and one of the men who felt the full force of it was Matt Henry as Jonny Bairstow smacked him into the River Trent. Now Henry could bring it all crashing down on a pitch in Nottingham that will dry after the heatwave and probably nip like the one at the Oval.

News.title: Thousands of migrants flee South Africa ahead of anti-foreigner ultimatum
News.content:
Despite the filthy conditions, more arrive each day.

“On June 30, we don’t know what will happen, but we are not safe here,” explains Hojane Mhone.

News.title: Undav is Germany’s unlikely World Cup hero who was playing semi-pro at 23
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Germany vs Ivory Coast from Toronto Stadium, with both teams looking to build on winning starts at the World Cup in North America.

Germany have all but secured their progression from the group-stage for the first time since they lifted the trophy in 2014 following their first 7-1 win since 2014. Though the semi-final dismantling of host nation Brazil 12 years ago will live longer in the memory, the swatting aside of newcomers Curacao on Sunday was the perfect start for Julian Nagelsmann’s men.

The four-time champions have not been widely tipped for another success this summer, but they are certainly building momentum under Naglesmann, with Sunday’s victory taking their winning run into double digits in a record dating back to September.

The seven-goal haul also meant they overtook Brazil as the leading scorers in World Cup history; a title that was lost after the Seleção’s 3-0 win over Haiti in the early hours of this morning, but one that can be restored with three goals of their own tonight.

However, chances will be harder to come by against Ivory Coast, a team ranked 53 places higher than Curacao and riding high after an impressive albeit fortuitous clean sheet against Ecuador in their opening game.

Manchester United’s Amad Diallo snatched victory for Emerse Faé’s side with a superb strike in the 90th minute after the South American side, previously unbeaten in two years, had struck the woodwork three times.

Though the pressure of progression is now all but lifted from Germany and Ivory Coast, tonight’s match is hugely significant in the battle to top Group E. The group-winners will face a third-placed team in the last 32, while finishing runners-up will set up a match against the second-placed side from Group I, which contains France, Senegal and Norway.

News.title: Rampant Netherlands tear Potter’s Sweden to pieces in World Cup rout
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Netherlands vs Sweden in Group F at the 2026 World Cup, a contest between two teams with contrasting strengths.

Sweden certainly pack a punch up front with Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres in tandem, while the Dutch possess a strong back four and one of the most technically proficient midfields in the tournament.

Despite the Netherlands’ apparent defensive strength, they were pegged back twice by a dangerous Japan side and had to settle for a 2-2 draw in their opening game.

There is plenty of scepticism back home about Ronald Koeman’s approach, and compared to the great Dutch sides of the past they look short on blue-chip attackers. Crysencio Summerville, Donyell Malen and Cody Gakpo is a decent front three, but there is no Arjen Robben, Dennis Bergkamp or Marco van Basten in the ranks this time.

Sweden and Graham Potter find themselves one positive result away from a place in the knockout stages, despite failing to win a single game in qualifying (Potter was not in charge for all of the campaign). It was only their Nations League results that earned them a place in the play-offs.

Yasin Ayari scored twice in a 5-1 victory over Tunisia, though they look certain to finish bottom of the group so the quality of opposition should be taken into account.

Potter said: “We’ll meet another top team at the weekend that’s one of the favourites for the competition, I would say, when you look at the players they have, the quality they have. So, it’s going to be a tough game.”

Asked about Isak and Gyokeres’s partnership, he added: “I think they complement each other very well. They bring different attributes, different qualities.

“Individually, of course, they’re top players. But I think together they can be a real threat. So the challenge for us is to make sure the team functions well and to get the best out of those two guys.”



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Saints’ Prem title built on English talent – and that is good news for Borthwick
News.content:
“This is a special week and we want to make sure that we enjoy that, but also stick to our guns and rely on what has got us to this point as a group,” Northampton boss Phil Dowson said. “We want to make the occasion special and the performance normal. So many finals are close affairs; we have had two great match-ups with Exeter already this season so I am sure Saturday will be no different.

“We know the quality of Chiefs. We were a long way ahead in that first game of the season and they came back at us, not too dissimilarly to how they did against Bath last weekend. The tenacity, cohesion, and belief that Exeter have has been on show throughout this season. The final is a brand-new game and we will need to be aware of those threats, but our focus is firmly on ourselves. We know the unity of our squad is a huge strength. We also know that you can train for these occasions and these environments; we have just got to trust that training when the pressure comes on.”

Exeter pulled off one of the most impressive comeback victories in recent Prem play-off history. Away from home at defending champions Bath, they found themselves 26-10 down at half-time, only to come back to win 27-26, holding out at the death on their own line for 40 phases. This is Exeter’s first Prem final since losing to Harlequins in 2021 and caps a remarkable turnaround over the last 12 months, having finished ninth in the Prem last season.

“The excitement of days like this, though, is also for some of the guys who have not been in big games like this before, so it is about them getting there and showing the best of themselves,” Exeter DOR Rob Baxter said. “The combination of that energy and emotional control, that will decide whether it is us or Northampton that secures it.

News.title: Rag-tag England on brink despite Root’s brilliance
News.content:
It is not a surprise England have been outclassed at the Oval when you compare the two team-sheets and a canny New Zealand side that looks much sharper for having played the first Test at Lord’s. In Matt Henry they have unerringly accurate bowler probing wobbly English defences and the giants Kyle Jamieson and Will O’Rourke who kept the heat on. Only Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue would get in the New Zealand attack and they would be fighting for Nathan Smith’s place, not replacing any of the other three.

A defeat here will be England’s sixth in their last eight Tests, the two wins coming on lottery pitches at the MCG and Lord’s. Stokes will return next week for the decider at Trent Bridge where for the first time England and New Zealand will meet on a fair pitch (you hope) and be at full strength. It is just whether England have the backbone to rally after such a torrid time. The past two weeks have felt like an Ashes tour falling apart and the futures of the coach and director of cricket, Rob Key, are on the line again.

Root has seen it all before and took the opportunity to play his way into the Test summer with a superb innings while Brook unfurled some sumptuous strokes in his half century before Henry pinned him down again. Jofra Archer gave England a lift with a fiery opening spell in the morning but New Zealand hung on and ground England down. They were all out just after lunch for 362 to set a target of 463 with nearly five sessions to go.

Sports.title: Incredible tale of lads who fled Britain for ’86 Mexico World Cup & never came back… as they reunite to cheer on England
Sports.content:
IT’S the kind of scheme you dream up with your mates in the pub after a few too many beers.

“We’ve all lost our jobs . . . rather than looking for new ones, why don’t we fly to the other side of the world and watch the World Cup?”





Nonsense, right? Especially if you have got kids and partners.

Not so for self-named “The Disco Firm” — a group of 20-somethings from the West Midlands.

It was June 1986 in Margaret Thatcher’s Britain. Three million people were jobless, and the unemployment rate nudged above ten per cent.

Wolves fans Garry Hardwicke, Gary Allen and Stuart Bates, from Stourbridge, and Birmingham City fan David Arnold, from Solihull, were among those out of work and down on their luck.

So they jumped on a plane to Mexico and watched all five of England’s games in one of the most memorable World Cups ever.

Shockingly, the foursome, who are the subject of new documentary Lost Down Mexico Way, arrived in the country not even knowing Spanish was the national language.

Gary, now 63, and living in Atlanta, told the programme he orchestrated the plan, but that the others were more than happy to go along with it.

Nicknamed Adder in those days, he recalls: “The Black Country was pretty grim back then. I was excited. One big, massive adventure for the taking. Mexico World Cup. Get in.



“We had never done anything like it before. I had about £500 saved up before I lost my job.”

Meanwhile, Stuart, who had not long lost his father, had another motivation — he had three Crown Court appearances at the time.

Gary says: “He’d just done three years out of a six-year stretch.



“He got done for robbing the local Post Office and then he got done for accidentally running down three Southampton fans down in the south coast watching the football.”

As the gang waited at Stourbridge train station with just one bag each and a few hundred pounds in their pockets, Gary explains that Garry, known as Rabbithead and who died in 2024 from pancreatitis, was late.

It was because he was sneaking out without telling his girlfriend Janet, who was also the mother of his three-year-old daughter Nicole.

Gary remembers: “He’d thrown his bag out the window, gone downstairs, told the missus he was nipping out for a pint of milk.

“Hope she wasn’t waiting for the milk for too long because he was gone for 12 years.”



He recalls that he was excited as the train pulled away from the platform, but Stuart appeared pensive.

Gary says: “He was looking back and back and back at the town and getting more emotional.

“I didn’t know it at the time that he was saying goodbye to England.”

Dad-of-four Stuart, now 63, who lives in Houston, Texas, and works in the car industry, says he was thinking, “Am I going to make this work? This is my salvation.

“We were watching Duran Duran videos filmed in Rio and Bowie filming in Australia and I knew I just wanted to travel.



“When the chance came, I just thought, ‘Why not?’, even though we knew nothing about Mexico as there wasn’t the internet.”

The four flew from Birmingham to Gatwick then 5,000 miles to San Antonio, in Texas, where they caught buses to Monterrey in Mexico.

Stuart says: “It was crazy, we had no clue.” And Gary adds their accommodation was “kind of dodgy”.



England’s first game of the tournament was a disappointing 1-0 defeat to Portugal at the Tecnologico Stadium in Monterrey.

After watching the match, the group headed north and crossed the border to South Padre Island, in Texas, for some sun. It was a turning point for Stuart.

He says: “I thought to myself I could stay here, I could get a job here and leave old Blighty.” But it was not just a time for reflection, as the group also partied hard.

Remembering an occasion in a bar, Stuart says: “We’re all in our early 20s, we’re all fit, we’re all dressed in tracksuits and England tops.

“People come and start talking to us. ‘Hey, are you the England soccer team?’. And one of the lads said, ‘Yeah, we’re the England football team’.



“So all these girls are coming up to us asking for autographs and someone comes up to me and, ‘Oh, who are you, sir? What’s your name?’.

“I said, ‘I’m Peter Shilton and he is Gary Lineker’.”

Gary adds: “All of a sudden they said, ‘Could the England team come on stage and take a bow.

“We were all looking and thinking, ‘They’re on about us here’.”

The men said they embraced their “fame”, climbing on stage to bow and signing autographs on napkins.



Gary adds: “It was the whole nine yards, it was brilliant.”

They also used their status as the “England squad” for more nefarious means.

Gary says: “This one cougar girl, a beautiful, beautiful stunner chats to Stuart and he says, ‘Yeah, I’m the goalkeeper. I’m Peter Shilton, watch out for me on TV’.

“So he gets off with her that night and we next see her in the morning.”

As well as romancing and partying, the lads got to see plenty of football.



England’s second match of the group stages was back in the same stadium in Monterrey. Again it was a disappointing result, 0-0 against Morocco.

This left them with a must-win match against Poland at the nearby Estadio Universitario in San Nicolas de los Garza.

Up stepped star striker Lineker to score a vital hat-trick — and England’s 3-0 win was enough to see them through to the last-16 knockout stages.



Another 3-0 victory, this time over Paraguay at the Azteca stadium in Mexico City, set up the now-infamous clash against Diego Maradona’s Argentina in the quarter-final.

Again in the Azteca, which also saw the opening game of the current World Cup, the lads were there to witness England’s controversial 2-1 defeat — and that Hand of God goal from Maradona.

Gary told The Times: “Even in the stadium it was clear [it was a handball], every person in the stadium could see what Maradona had done — apart from the referee.”

The tense match took place just four years after the UK had defeated Argentina in the Falklands War and the stadium was packed with Argentinian fans.

Afterwards, Garry was chased by rival supporters. He stumbled off a bridge and ended up in hospital for a few weeks with a fractured skull and broken arms and legs.



Meanwhile, David was stabbed in the leg with a flag pole.

While the match marked the end of England’s run in tournament, it did not mean that the four friends were coming home to the Black Country. David ended up staying in Monterrey, eventually running a school as a head teacher.

The other three settled in the US after moving to South Padre to find work.



Gary, who now lives in Atlanta and has two children, says: “You could get a job anywhere. I had three jobs in the first three or four weeks.”

Now retired, he went on to build a sewage and drain equipment business that had an annual turnover of £15.1million.

Garry also lived in Atlanta as a painter. Before his death, he contacted his daughter Nicole, who was in Huddersfield, on Facebook.

They had formed a positive relationship, but veterinary receptionist Nicole, 42, told reporters that her mum Janet had still not forgiven her ex for hopping on a flight to Mexico without telling her.

She added: “My mother is still fuming about it now.”



Meanwhile, Garry’s sister Fiona was no less honest, saying: “Garry used to say, ‘I can’t look after a goldfish, let alone a child’.”

With the World Cup currently back in Mexico, as well as Canada and the US, Gary reunited with Stuart last week to watch England’s opening game, a 4-2 win over Croatia at the Dallas Stadium in Texas

Ever-cheeky England fan Gary and his son even managed to gatecrash a Croatian VIP box, where they necked free booze and food before settling in to their £2,200 seats.

Gary and Stuart also reunited with Steve “Texas” Dawson, from Dallas, who they met on their first trip to Texas in 1986.

Gary says: “It was amazing to see the lads because it had certainly been a while.



“The place was absolutely packed around the stadium. All the bars were rammed but once you got inside it was just incredible.

“It is the best stadium I have ever watched England in and they’ve certainly come a long way since Mexico ’86.

“Back then they were all raw and rough, now they are absolutely state-of-the-art futuristic things with air-conditioning.

“Once we got inside it was much easier to get a drink. There was a bar every 20ft and a restaurant every 50ft.”

He says it was “special” going to the game with his old mates. Head teacher David, who still lives in Monterrey and has four children with his wife, could not join them.



Gary adds: “Myself, Stuart and Steve had never all been to an England game together.

“Afterwards we went back to the hotel and stayed up until 2am having a few beers and chatting and reminiscing.

“The game was absolutely fantastic, I think we’re really rolling now and we’ll go deep into the tournament.

“The fans were great and the atmosphere was something else around the stadium.

“Back in ’86 you were herded around and treated like trouble- makers, but it really is a carnival atmosphere.



“I hope England can carry on performing like that and we can go all the way.”

THOMAS TUCHEL repeatedly shouted “wake up” at Djed Spence during an England training session.

The Three Lions have been busy at their Kansas City HQ preparing for Tuesday’s clash with Ghana.

Sports.title: Emma Hayes pays emotional tribute to late dad and sends clear message live on ITV in divisive World Cup tactic slot
Sports.content:
EMMA HAYES has paid a heartfelt tribute to her dad on Father’s Day.

The USWNT boss made the gesture live on ITV during their World Cup coverage of Belgium v Iran.





ITV drafted the former Chelsea Women’s boss in for her expert tactical analysis.

And while she continues to act as a regular pundit during the pre-game, half-time and after-game broadcast, during matches she is also working as a tactics expert.

During the controversial hydration breaks introduced by Fifa, Hayes has been seen breaking down the tactics of the game.

But as she finished off her segment for the Belgium v Iran game, the 49-year-old paid a heartfelt tribute to her late dad, Sid, who died in 2023, on Father’s Day.

She said: “One last thing, happy Father’s Day to everyone at home.

“I know it’s a great day and it’s also my father’s heavenly birthday today and I want to say one thing to your dad up in heaven.

“Thank you for giving me so much confidence to have the opportunity to do this and so I leave you with this beautiful view.”

Hayes then turned around to reveal the text, “she will change the world,” on the back of her jacket.



Sid Hayes was a major supporter of women’s football and played a major role in building Arsenal Women into one of the biggest team’s in the country and setting up Regent’s Park youth leagues.

He died at the age of 82 after a battle with lung cancer.

However, fans remained split over Hayes role on ITV during the hydration breaks.

One fan said: “Fair play Emma Hayes, she knew exactly what she was doing there. That will have got the misogynist trolls so angry and she loves it.”

A second said: “Emma Hayes not content with being bloody epic, she’s now goading the trolling bigots with her jacket and Father’s Day message. Things you love to see.”



A third added: “Emma Hayes dropping more unreal analysis, a beautiful tribute to her father and turning round to end with a jacket that reads ‘she will change the world’. Impeccable, incredible.”

Another said: “What is this nonsense man.”

A fifth said: “You got to rate Emma Hayes.”

Sports.title: Curacao’s World Cup draw tinged with sadness as keeper pays tribute to tragic former player who suddenly died
Sports.content:
CURACAO’S World Cup fairytale was tinged with sadness after hero goalkeeper Eloy Room paid tribute to former team-mate Jairzinho Pieter

Room, 37, produced one of the greatest goalkeeping displays in World Cup history as minnows Curacao held Ecuador to a stunning 0-0 draw in Kansas City.





The veteran stopper made a staggering 15 saves – the most ever recorded across a 90-minute World Cup match.

Only former USA keeper Tim Howard has ever made more in a tournament game – stopping 16 shots against Belgium after extra-time in 2014.

But while Curacao celebrated the first World Cup point in the Caribbean island’s history, memories turned to former international goalkeeper Pieter, who died in 2019 after suffering a cardiac arrest while away on international duty.

Pieter, aged just 31, passed away at Curacao’s team hotel in Haiti on the eve of a Concacaf Nations League clash.



The keeper had reportedly felt unwell before collapsing.

It was later confirmed Pieter had suffered a heart attack.

Pieter spent his club career in Curacao and was a respected figure within the national team setup.

One man who knew him well was Room.



The veteran goalkeeper has continued to carry the memory of his former colleague throughout his international career.

After his heroic display against Ecuador, Room dedicated the performance to Pieter – holding up a shirt with the message: “This is for you, pure love from Curacao.”

Speaking after the game, Room said: “Jairzinho is always with us. We never forget him. He was part of this journey and part of this family.”

Curacao’s incredible result also left veteran boss Dick Advocaat, 78, visibly emotional at full-time.



The former Netherlands manager looked close to tears as his side, representing a nation of little more than 150,000 people, kept alive hopes of reaching the knockout stages at their first-ever World Cup finals.

Six days after suffering a brutal 7-1 defeat to Germany on their tournament debut, Curacao responded in sensational fashion.

Room repeatedly denied Ecuador, producing save after save as the South Americans piled on the pressure.

Next up is a showdown with Ivory Coast in Philadelphia, while Ecuador face Germany in New York.

Sports.title: People just realising non-League club’s little-known role in careers of all three England goalkeepers at World Cup 2026
Sports.content:
IF at any point in history England’s top three goalkeepers had passed through the same club, some obvious candidates would spring to mind.

But the conveyor belt of goalkeeping talent feeding this generation does not come from Manchester United, Liverpool or Arsenal.





It comes from a plucky non-League side trying to scrap their way back to the EFL.

Jordan Pickford, Dean Henderson and James Trafford would not be the stoppers they are today without… Carlisle United.

All three grew up not far from the Scottish border and honed their skills at the Cumbrian club.

Henderson, 29, was there first, signing as a schoolboy in 2005 after catching the eye of scout James Tose at a local community event.

Tose told BBC Sport: “We’re standing there and all these kids keep lining up taking penalties and Dean keeps saving them all.

“There might have been 18 or 19 penalties. No-one was scoring.

“I think I took a penalty myself and he saved that too.

“Then I remembered meeting his mum and dad. They were over six foot and I thought, ‘Wow, he’s good in goal and there’s a chance he might be tall too’.”

It took some convincing for Henderson to give up his dreams of being an outfield player.

But once he had come to terms with a potential career between the sticks, he gave it all he had.

Eric Kinder, an ex-goalkeeping coach with Carlisle’s youth teams, recalled: “The first time I met him was during half-term, he must have been 13 or 14, and he kept pestering me to train with the under-18s.

“I would say, ‘You’re too young, you’re too small’. But eventually I let him have a go.

“So now we’ve got two 18-year-old centre-forwards smashing balls at him from 12 and 18 yards. They’re hitting him in the face and in the stomach.

He said: “As a player you could call him an introvert, takes it all in, not the life and soul of the party but that’s not a bad thing, you see a calmness to his play.”



Trafford, 23, remains at City, where he is stuck behind Gianluigi Donnarumma, but many see him as a future England No1.

The current No1, Pickford, had a more fleeting association with Carlisle.

Brunton Park was an important loan destination for the 32-year-old in 2014, while he was still on the books at boyhood club Sunderland.



There, he took his first steps in League One football, laying the foundations for a career boasting almost 400 Premier League appearances and 85 England caps.

Benson, who was at Carlisle at the time, explained: “In Jordan you see reliability and robustness first and foremost.

“I remember one game in particular, we were playing at Deepdale against Preston.

Sports.title: Spain 4 Saudi Arabia 0: ‘Sad’ Spanish lay down World Cup marker as Lamine Yamal makes it 33 unbeaten with crushing win
Sports.content:
AN angry and upset Spain tore through Saudi Arabia to finally lay down a World Cup marker.

After their goalless Cape Verde debacle the European champions put their foot down to remind everyone just why they are one of the favourites.





Luis de la Fuente described his players as having been stung, Martin Zubimendi said the squad were sad.

Whatever emotion was coursing through them, it worked as a ferocious first half, sparked by Lamine Yamal’s first World Cup goal, set up a dream day in Atalanta – Spain now 33 unbeaten.

It would be easy to say it was only Saudi Arabia, but everyone thought that about Cape Verde.

Spain pulled off perhaps the most complete 45 minutes of any nation in North America so far this summer and could afford to give their first half goalscorers, Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal, a rest as early as the break. Marc Cucurella added a fourth shortly after the break.



Saudi Arabia had every right to be upset with Cape Verde. The African islanders poked the bear and the Saudis paid the price.

For the first 25 minutes they were trampled like a hopeless Matador against a raging bull.

De la Fuente, a big bullfighting fan celebrating his birthday, hinted that he might keep Yamal back to make another appearance off the bench as he continues to recover from a hamstring injury sustained in April.

But the Spanish boss sent his talisman out from the off – and he was causing trouble after just 40 seconds, twisting and turning down the right before delivering dangerous crosses.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

It then took him just ten minutes to open his account on football’s grandest stage.

Yamal’s finish, sliding in at the far post, was simple, but the flowing move before and the fine, fizzed ball across goal from Oyarzabal would have unpicked any side.

Every now and then it is worth a reminder that this ridiculous lad, having already shone on the way to winning the Euros two years ago, is just 18. A teenager delivering despite the hopes of a nation bearing down on his shoulders.

Oyarzabal, the Real Sociedad striker, was lambasted for failing to even get a touch of the ball in the first 30 minutes of Spain’s painful opener.



Two goals and an assist inside the opening 24 this time around should just about make up for that, his brace delivered inside three minutes which ended any hope of an upset.

Spain’s second was as ugly as the opener was attractive.

Saudi Arabia failed to clear a Spain corner with the ball falling to Dani Olmo. The Barcelona man hooked a horrible shot which was travelling back towards the corner. The Saudi back line managed a block, but Aymeric Laporte was straight in to nod it towards Oyarzabal to prod in.



Spain’s dogged poacher persisted, capping off a much more accomplished move minutes later.

Tottenham’s Pedro Porro lifted a ball to the far post where Cucurella cushioned for Olmo to head towards the far post and onto the foot of Oyarzabal for a tap-in.

Saudi Arabia had been dismantled all before the farce of a hydration break in an air-conditioned stadium.



Not that the break helped them too much. Before the half was out, keeper Mohammed Al Owais stupidly tried to play short to his right only to pick out Oyarzabal who so nearly bagged his hat-trick, whipping an outside of the boot effort onto the top of the bar.

La Roja eased off for a time, effectively put their feet up as they knocked the ball around struggling Saudis desperate for at least a kick.

Spain had their opponents pinned back throughout. While it looked like a cricket score was on the cards early on, De la Fuente’s men were more than happy to tick over for the rest of the game – though a fourth was added early in the second half.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cucurella, the new Real Madrid man, saw a thunderous strike from the far post saved by Al Owais, only for it to cannon in off the back of Hassan Al Tambakti.

But from there the Spaniards sailed on, aside from a Ferran Torres disallowed goal, all eyes on their final group game against Uruguay and whatever may lay ahead – slippers on and pipes out for the remainder in Atlanta.

Sports.content:
England sent warning from Ghana fan

Andy Lines, in Boston

The owner of the only Ghana restaurant in Boston warned England today: “We’re going to beat you.”

And he said that: “England may have Declan Rice but we’ve got jollof rice.” Will Yakah, 30, was referring to his country’s popular national dish.

And the Manchester United fanatic invited any of the tens of thousands of Three Lions supporters to come and visit his fast food restaurant RedRed to enjoy a beer and some traditional Ghanian food.

He said: “When the World Cup draw was made - we were so excited. You can only dream of drawing England, with all their Premier League stars, in the World Cup - not only in the US but here in Boston.

“We’ve been looking forward to this for months. Ghana has never lost the second group match of any World Cup tournament we have ever played in! “Watch out England - we’re going to win. Jollof rice is much more popular than Declan Rice in Ghana - even though he plays for Arsenal … one of Ghanians favourite teams!”

England play Ghana at Boston stadium in the town of Foxborough on Tuesday evening.

Both the Three Lions and Ghana won their opening matches - which ever side wins is guaranteed a coveted place in the knockout stages.

Will’s restaurant serves up traditional dishes like jollof rice, waakye, kelewele - spicy fried plantain - and puff puff at the restaurant in Nubian Square in the suburb of Roxbury. The area has a powerful murals on the walls paying tribute to civil rights heroes like Rosa Parks and Martin Luther King.

He said: “There are so many Ghana players with links to the Premier League. Members of the current squad include Manchester City’s Antoine Semenyo, Mohammed Kudus who is with Tottenham Hotspur and Andre Ayew who played for Nottingham Forest and West Ham United. “And of course our new manager is Carlos Queiroz who was Alex Ferguson’s number two at Man United for so long.” He said many Ghanians have an English team. “I’m Man United but many of my friends are Arsenal,” he said. “And there are lots of Chelsea fans because of the great former Ghana player Michael Essien.” Will was born in the capital Accra but moved to the US 12 years ago He is co-owner of the restaurant which has been open for three years.

He actually has a stand inside the Fifa Fanfest in central Boston but is only allowed to serve food there. here’s a reason for that - Fifa makes the money on the drinks. A coke is £5.50 and a beer £10 there but just £1.50 and £7 at Will’s place a ten minute journey away.

The town of Worcester just outside Boston is home to the second largest population of Ghanians in the United States.

Lucas Bergvall makes Tottenham transfer stance clear after Tonali and Mateus Fernandes rumours

Tottenham Hotspur have been linked with a number of midfielders this summer, including Sandro Tonali and Mateus Ferna

View 2 Images Lucas Bergvall wants to leave Spurs (Image: Lewis Storey - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Lucas Bergvall has told Tottenham Hotspur of his intentions to leave the club this summer. The 20-year-old, who only made the switch to North London from Djurgarden in 2024 in an £8.5million deal, found consistent playing time hard to come by during the closing stages of 2025/26, predominantly featuring as a second-half substitute after Roberto De Zerbi's arrival.

‌



And now, the Athletic report that the Sweden international - who is presently representing his country at the 2026 World Cup in North America - is seeking a new challenge elsewhere. While the midfielder has previously caught the eye of clubs including Chelsea and Aston Villa, Spurs showed no willingness at the time to part ways with him.

‌



Whether either side remain interested in his services is yet to be determined. Considering how expensive the midfield market has become this summer, a transfer for Bergvall - who remains under contract until 2031 - is unlikely to be straightforward.

‌

The Lilywhites ended up 17th in the Premier League table last term, barely escaping relegation to the Championship on the final day of the season with a 1-0 victory over Everton.

‌

Sports.title: Ex-England star Ashley Cole quits first managerial job after just EIGHT games
Sports.content:
Ex-England star Ashley Cole quits first managerial job after just EIGHT games

Ashley Cole was appointed by Italian side Cesena in March to mark his first managerial role after years in coaching, but following a poor end to the season, he's decided to leave

View 2 Images Ashley Cole is already looking for pastures new (Image: Gabriele Maricchiolo/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Ashley Cole has decided to quit as manager of Italian side Cesena after only eight games in charge. Cole, 45, was appointed by the Serie B club in March, stepping into his first managerial role.

‌



The former England left-back and Premier League legend signed a contract until the end of the 2025-26 season with the aim of finishing in the play-offs. Under Cole, Cesena managed to win just one of their eight games.

‌



Brief discussions over his future took place at the end of the season, but according to various reports, Cole has now chosen to leave. The ex-Chelsea and Arsenal star took charge with Cesena eighth in the Serie B table, occupying the league's final play-off spot as they aimed to reach the top flight for the first time since 2015.

‌



Cole's side ended up finishing in 11th, recording one win, three draws and four defeats in their final eight games. His appointment, along with that of former Chelsea academy coach Jack Mesure, was met with scepticism from Cesena's fan base.

Chelsea swap deal for £163million stars proposed as huge transfer given green light READ MORE :

The club had sacked Michele Mignani, who'd been in charge for nearly two years, after losing eight of his last 13 games. At the time, it was reported that Cesena sporting director Filippo Fusco disagreed with the decision to sack Mignani, while some players were said to have been in tears upon learning the news.

‌



American co-owner Mike Melby was a driving force behind Cesena's move for Cole, having gotten to know the three-time Premier League winner from his time with LA Galaxy. Cole is expected to be on the lookout for his next coaching position.

He worked with Frank Lampard at both Chelsea and Everton, and alongside Wayne Rooney at Birmingham City. Cole also assisted Lee Carsley during his time as interim England manager.

Will Ashley Cole have a successful career as a manager? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Ashley Cole only managed one win as Cesena manager (Image: Gabriele Maricchiolo/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

His wife, Sharon Canu, is from Italy, and they met during Cole's spell playing for Roma. "It was always in our plans to live in Italy because we love the food and the calmness of the country," Cole told the Guardian in April.

"She [Canu] told me the fans here are passionate about their team and their city. I had to embrace that, understand what makes them tick, so we can represent them properly."

Article continues below

Cole went on to say: "I feel ready and that I should be a head coach. I am definitely thankful to Cesena for the opportunity, but I have more than enough experience."

Sports.title: Spain send emphatic reminder to World Cup rivals as England's villain bags brace
Sports.content:
Spain send emphatic reminder to World Cup rivals as England's villain bags brace

SPAIN 4-0 SAUDI ARABIA: Mikel Oyarzabal struck twice while Lamine Yamal scored his first goal at a World Cup to finally give Luis de la Fuente's men liftoff in Group H

View 3 Images Spain hammered Saudi Arabia in Atlanta (Image: Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images)

They're European champions for a reason, you know? After Monday's shock 0-0 draw with Cape Verde, a fired-up Spain had a statement to make.

‌



If there were any concerns that this would be another painstaking affair for Luis de la Fuente's side, they were quickly dispelled inside 24 minutes, as Saudi Arabia were put to the sword. Lamine Yamal's first World Cup goal opened the floodgates before a brace from Mikel Oyarzabal put the game out of sight.

‌



England fans will reluctantly recognise the Real Sociedad forward, who scored the winning goal against Gareth Southgate's team in the final of Euro 2024. Celebrating his 65th birthday, De la Fuente made four changes to La Roja's starting XI and he was vindicated with victory.

‌



In a more settled-looking line-up, out came Marcos Llorente, Fabian Ruiz, Gavi and Ferran Torres, and in came Pedro Porro, Dani Olmo, Alex Baena and Yamal. Square pegs for square holes.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

UEFA make decision on hydration breaks for Euro 2028 in UK and Ireland READ MORE :

World Cup LIVE: Spain vs Saudi Arabia updates as three teams kicked out after FIFA decision READ MORE :

Yamal's simple finish with 10 minutes on the clock won't be going in his career goal catalogue, but it was the kind of smart run and back-post tap-in that he'll need to master if he wants to put up prime Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo-level numbers from the wing.

‌



It was a similar story for Oyarzabal's brace, ghosting behind the Saudi defence on two occasions to bag a brace in the space of three minutes. With an assist to boot, it was just what the doctor ordered for Spain's No.21, who had a frustrating night against Cape Verde. Flashing a shot across goal before half-time, Oyarzabal was hungry for this third.

Will Spain win the World Cup? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 3 Images Lamine Yamal scored his first World Cup goal to break the deadlock (Image: Juan Luis Diaz/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



But the 29-year-old was robbed of the chance to score an historic World Cup hat-trick by his manager. De la Fuente subbed both him and Yamal at break, clearly with an eye on Saturday's Group H closer against Uruguay.

Yamal's fitness remains a concern for Spain, having missed the last knockings of Barcelona's season because of a hamstring injury. And when you've got such depth in attack, why not use it?

Within four minutes of the restart, it was 4-0. Marc Cucurella's shot was initially saved by Saudi goalkeeper Mohammed Al-Owais, only for the ball to cannon back off Hassan Al-Tambakti and into the of the net.

‌



View 3 Images Mikel Oyarzabal was denied a hat-trick after being substituted (Image: Juan Luis Diaz/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

With three points all but secured, Spain's substitutes were able to strut their stuff. Arsenal's Mikel Merino threaded a perfectly weighted ball into the path of Torres, who prodded his effort wide. After a tepid last half-hour, the former Manchester City star thought that he'd finally scored in stoppage time, only for VAR to rule his goal out for offside following a lengthy review.

Saudi Arabia have no reason to be down, though, knowing that a win over Cape Verde would almost certainly send them through to the last 32. The Green Falcons have only reached the knockout stages of a World Cup once in their seven appearances, reaching the round of 16 on debut in 1998. Georgios Donis' side will be out to make more history next weekend.

Sports.title: Trevoh Chalobah opens up on unique Thomas Tuchel relationship after World Cup call-up
Sports.content:
Trevoh Chalobah opens up on unique Thomas Tuchel relationship after World Cup call-up

Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah was on holiday in New York without any kit when he received a message from Thomas Tuchel asking him to join England's World Cup squad

View 4 Images Trevoh Chalobah was called up after Tino Livramento's injury (Image: Eddie Keogh/The FA via Getty Images)

Trevoh Chalobah says his England World Cup call-up is his “number one” career highlight.

‌



The Chelsea defender admitted he was holidaying in New York but deliberately went to America because Thomas Tuchel told him to “stay ready.”

‌



Chalobah, 26, was initially left out of Tuchel’s 26-man squad but got the call after Tino Livramento suffered an injury on the eve of the tournament - and he immediately jumped at the chance.

‌



Centre-half Chalobah revealed:

England boss Tuchel texted him while he was sightseeing in Times Square - but he missed the message for two hours

He had to get emergency kit sent because he had given all his boots and shirts away in a competition

His “banter” relationship with Tuchel - and how the England boss tried to sign him when he was in charge at Bayern Munich

Never giving up on making it - and how his faith helped him through after he was relegated to Chelsea’s “bomb squad”

Fulfilling a dream of playing at a World Cup after posting a tweet which read “One Day” in 2018 alongside a picture of the trophy

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

‌



England star Reece James gives honest reaction to Marc Cucurella's Chelsea exit READ MORE :

Pundit apologises after telling World Cup star he shouldn't leave for birth of his child READ MORE :

Chalobah said: “When we got the news at the end of the season, whether we were selected or not, he said ‘you were close.’ I was disappointed that I didn’t make it but he did say ‘stay ready.’

“So I managed to have a few sessions here and there but really it was about enjoying my holiday, I flew up to New York and was meant to go to Los Angeles after that but obviously had to cut it short when I got the message on Monday.

“I was literally in Times Square. I went to the shops to get something. It was when I got back to my hotel I saw Thomas had texted but it was two hours before. I wasn’t on my phone and my heart just stopped.

‌



“He texted me and said ‘Hi, Trevoh, are you free for a call?’ I just knew straight away. I called on video and he was smiling and said: ‘I have got some news for you.’ I was just over the moon.”

View 4 Images Trevoh Chalobah has settled into the England squad (Image: Eddie Keogh/The FA via Getty Images)

Chalobah flew across to Kansas City while the rest of the squad went to Dallas for their first game with Croatia but they did set up a behind-closed-doors game the next day to help him and others get match sharpness.

‌



But there was one problem. “Funnily enough, I gave away my boots at the end of the season in a giveaway,” he smiled. “My sponsors Reebok were sending some more across with my personal trainer but we had to speed up the process. But my first training session was on Saturday.”

Having to wait a few extra days - the squad was given a day off on Friday - was no problem bearing in mind he has waited this long for a chance. Chalobah worked up a sweat playing padel with teammates Ivan Toney and Ezri Konsa and is adjusting.

And Chalobah has a big supporter in his corner. Tuchel gave him his debut for Chelsea in 2021, gave him his debut for England against Senegal in June 2025 and even tried to sign him for Bayern Munich.

‌



View 4 Images Thomas Tuchel and Trevoh Chalobah have a long history (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

Chalobah said: “Yeah, when I was at Chelsea, he tried to bring me to Bayern. We've always had that special relationship. He's the one that gave me my debut in 2021 in my breakthrough season at Chelsea. My England debut as well. So we've always had that.

“We have that strong connection. Yeah, he’s really fun! When I was at Chelsea, he was really demanding, which helped me. We have that really fun, banter relationship and I love it.”

‌



Chalobah has had his fair share of ups and downs in his career. He joined Chelsea aged eight, has been out on loan at Ipswich, Huddersfield, Lorient and Crystal Palace and his face has not always fitted at Stamford Bridge.

Now he is up against it again. He knows he is in the United States to be part of the squad and may not get a start. But he laughed when reminded of a similar late England call-up before the 2002 World Cup. That time, Trevor Sinclair was cut from the squad, went on holiday but was recalled because of an injury and ended up starting against Brazil in the quarter final.

View 4 Images Trevoh Chalobah went to New York in hope of receiving a call-up (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Chalobah said: “In my career I’ve always been coming in – maybe not seen as playing – but then I always end up managing to play. It starts in training, just give my all, make sure I'm ready when called upon and I believe I can play a big part.

“I know the player I am. I know how far I've come. I know what I've been through, so I can't allow those moments to define who I am, or just have that disbelief — I have that faith.

“Faith has been one of my key things. Because of my faith, I know that those moments won't define me or who I am and I know what I've been through. I just use those moments as fuel to always prove people wrong and I love it.”

‌



And that tweet from 2018 which went viral after his World Cup call-up last week. He was out on loan at Ipswich at the time - and is now realising his dream.

He added: “I remember I was on loan at Ipswich that year and that was when the World Cup was in Russia. And it has always been a dream and that day I decided to tweet it. I obviously believed one day hopefully I’d make it.

“For me this is number one in my career, especially because I didn’t expect it. I think that is the beautiful thing about it, when you didn’t expect it and to get a call like that shows that obviously when you think all is lost or it’s not going to happen, that tweet came true.”

Sports.title: Donald Trump's terror as World Cup fans chant Epstein songs in ultimate humiliation for US President
Sports.content:
Donald Trump's terror as World Cup fans chant Epstein songs in ultimate humiliation for US President

EXCLUSIVE: Donald Trump is facing a World Cup headache as viral chants linking him to Jeffrey Epstein spread among English-speaking fans, raising questions over whether he will attend matches or even present the trophy at the final

View 4 Images Donald Trump and FIFA president Gianni Infantino pose with the World Cup trophy in the Oval Office ahead of the tournament (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump may not attend a World Cup match involving an English-speaking team, after brutal fan chants linking the president to his old pal Jeffrey Epstein went viral.

‌



Concern is understood to be so high that questions are being asked about whether the US leader will present the trophy at the July 19 final, amid fears over what supporters could sing should he appear. White House officials are claimed to be attempting to shield Trump from the hostility on the terraces, particularly from fans of English-speaking nations.

‌



Supporters from England, Scotland, Australia and New Zealand have all created songs that now echo through bars before matches and inside stadiums during games. A source said: "There isn't a fan alive who doesn't know how fragile Trump's ego is. In recent months, he has had to contend with widespread booing whenever he attends major sporting events in America, but this is another level entirely.

‌



View 4 Images Australian fans at the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

“New Yorkers were furious when he turned up at the recent Knicks basketball game. But World Cup supporters are taking it to a whole new level, linking Trump to his friendship with Epstein and to his appearance in Epstein-related files.

"His staff are in crisis mode trying to prevent the President from being exposed to the chants in person, and that includes avoiding matches involving English-speaking teams."

‌



The Mirror understands lead broadcasters have already been made aware of the chants being heard at matches. Fans are drawing attention to Trump's long-documented friendship with Epstein, the paedophile who died in a New York jail cell in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex-trafficking charges.

The pair moved in the same social circles throughout the 1980s and 1990s and were photographed together on numerous occasions. In a 2002 interview with New York magazine, Trump described Epstein as a "terrific guy" and said he was "a lot of fun to be with".

The president has since sought to distance himself from his former friend, saying the pair fell out years before Epstein's criminal convictions and insisting he barred him from Mar-a-Lago.

‌



The issue has returned to the political spotlight because of continuing controversy surrounding the release of Epstein-related court documents and investigative files. Trump's name, along with those of numerous public figures, has appeared in released records, although inclusion in such documents is not evidence of criminal conduct or wrongdoing.

Nevertheless, the association remains politically toxic. Many of the chants circulating around World Cup venues directly reference Epstein, his crimes and Trump's past relationship with him.

One Washington insider said: "For opponents of Trump, Epstein has become shorthand for a story that refuses to go away. Football supporters are seizing on that. Whether the White House likes it or not, they have found a chant that instantly gets a reaction because everyone knows exactly what it refers to."

‌



View 4 Images England fans get behind their side at the World Cup, many chanting about Trump's links to Epstein (Image: Getty Images)

In the build-up to the tournament, Trump was warmly embraced by FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who presented him with football's governing body's first-ever 'Peace Prize' at the World Cup draw. FIFA said the award was given to a person who had "taken exceptional and extraordinary actions for peace" and had "united people across the world". Weeks later, Trump ordered military strikes against Iran.

Infantino has made several visits to the White House and has maintained a close relationship with the President.

‌



Trump has yet to attend a single World Cup match despite the United States hosting the tournament, an absence that has raised eyebrows. While White House aides have publicly cited scheduling commitments, Trump's decision to skip the United States' opening game was highly unusual for a host-nation leader.

Attention is now turning to whether he will attend later fixtures as a growing number of supporters adopt chants referencing Epstein.

Australian fans were among the first to generate headlines after videos of thousands singing anti-Trump songs spread rapidly across social media. Clips filmed in World Cup host cities have since been viewed millions of times online.

‌



The chants have become one of the unexpected stories of the tournament, highlighting how many supporters outside America view the President. While host nations traditionally use World Cups as a showcase for political leaders, Trump has remained largely out of sight. Instead, senior administration figures have represented the White House at fixtures and tournament events.

View 4 Images Donald Trump received a FIFA peace medal from Gianni Infantino, just weeks before he ordered the bombing of Iran

Secretary of State Marco Rubio was among those attending America's opener while Trump remained in Washington. Controversial Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has also attended matches and attracted significant attention from the crowd.

Article continues below

Video posted online from the United States-Australia match in Seattle appeared to show Kennedy being loudly booed by sections of supporters when shown on stadium screens. The reaction reflects the political mood hanging over the tournament. Trump has spent months promoting the World Cup as evidence of America's global standing and influence. Yet football's crowds have proved a far less welcoming audience than the rallies where he is accustomed to receiving adulation.

The Washington insider added: "Unlike carefully managed campaign rallies, international football supporters are unpredictable at best and care nothing for political sensitivities. The issue is particularly acute with English-speaking supporters because their chants are instantly understood by American audiences and television viewers alike. As the tournament moves into the knockout stages, the possibility of England or Scotland making a deep run is becoming an increasing concern for those charged with keeping Trump calm."

Sports.title: Bergvall asks to leave Tottenham
Sports.content:
Sweden midfielder Lucas Bergvall has asked to leave Tottenham Hotspur this summer.

The 20-year-old, who is currently with his country at the World Cup, has made the club aware of his wish to leave Spurs in search for a fresh start and concerns over regular first-team football.

Bergvall only played 112 minutes of football under Roberto De Zerbi, starting one of the Italian's six games in charge and featuring mainly as a substitute.

He joined Spurs from Swedish club Djurgarden in the 2024 winter window and his contract runs until June 2031.

Before joining Spurs, Barcelona were interested in Bergvall but he chose Tottenham, despite holding talks with Deco.

Spurs are pushing for reinforcements in midfield, and had an £80m bid for Sandro Tonali rebuffed by Newcastle on Saturday.

Sky Sports reporter Michael Bridge:

Never again. That was the promise made by Tottenham chief executive Vinai Venkatesham and non-executive chairman Peter Charrington after narrowly avoiding relegation from the Premier League.

There was a lot of criticism aimed at the Spurs board and sporting director Johan Lange after a disappointing January transfer window which left the team looking slim. It looked even more slim when the injuries started to pile up.

The promise from the Spurs hierarchy is that they are going to be stronger and they are going to back Roberto De Zerbi, who they have wanted to bring to the club for a long time. Even Daniel Levy, who left as former executive chairman a year ago, wanted to hire De Zerbi.

Now they've finally got him, and after he pulled off the miracle of keeping Spurs up, they want to back him by signing the players he wants. Jan Paul van Hecke, who De Zerbi worked with at Brighton, has already been brought in for £52m.

Read full feature here

Tottenham begin their 2026/27 Premier League season with a trip to Brentford on August 22, live on Sky Sports.

The Saturday 5.30pm kick-off at the Gtech Community Stadium will be the start of Roberto De Zerbi's first full season in charge of Spurs, who escaped relegation last season after a second consecutive 17th-placed finish.

Following the season-opening London derby, Tottenham host Newcastle in their first home game of the season on August 29.

Sports.title: Serena Williams receives final Wimbledon women's singles wild card
Sports.content:
Serena Williams has been handed the final Wimbledon singles wild card into the women's main draw as she prepares for her Grand Slam comeback.

The seven-time ⁠Wimbledon singles champion was ‌already assured of a return ‌to the championships for the first time in four ⁠years after ​accepting a doubles ​wild card with ​sister Venus.

Now the 44-year-old American legend will ‌make a stunning ​return to singles after being handed ​the final wild card by the All England ​Club on ⁠Sunday.

"This ​is not a drill," the tournament wrote in a ‌post on its Instagram account.

Williams, widely-regarded as the greatest female tennis player ‌of all time, last played a singles match at Wimbledon as a wild card in 2022, losing to Harmony Tan in round one.

After that ‌year's US Open she said she would "evolve away from tennis" although never officially retired.

Williams first appeared at Wimbledon in ​1998, reaching the singles third round.

She won the title for ​the first time in 2002, beating older sister Venus in ⁠the final, and went on to become the dominant force in the women's game, spending a combined total of 319 weeks as the WTA ⁠world No 1.

Williams added singles crowns in ​2003, 2009, 2010, 2012, 2015 and 2016 and also won ​six doubles titles at the grass-court major with Venus.

Serena has been practising at Wimbledon having posted a video on Instagram on Thursday showing her at Wimbledon's Aorangi Park practice courts along with daughters Olympia and Adira.

The American ended nearly four years away from the match court last week, winning her first contest at Queen's alongside Victoria Mboko before the Canadian's unfortunate injury curtailed their run.

She then headed to Berlin but suffered a first-round loss at the WTA Tour event playing with Karolina Muchova.

Wild cards are handed out by tournament organisers to players whose rankings do not permit automatic entry and are usually reserved for home ⁠players, those with illustrious career records or high-profile players ​returning from injury.

Why Serena is the GOAT

Over the course of her game-changing career to date, Williams, who is now 44 years, nine months old, spent 319 weeks as the WTA world No 1.



Her haul of 73 singles titles, including 23 Grand Slam trophies won over an 18-season period, is the Open era record.



The winner of 39 major titles overall, as well as multiple Olympic medals, she remains the only player to achieve a ‘career Golden Slam’ in singles and doubles (meaning she won both events at all four majors as well as the Olympic Games) and is the prize money leader in women’s sports.



Murray not surprised by Williams' Wimbledon return

Image: Andy Murray and Serena Williams played in the mixed doubles together at Wimbledon in 2019

Andy Murray revealed he was not surprised by Williams' return to Wimbledon after a conversation between the pair at last year's Miami Open.

Murray, who played alongside Williams in the 2019 Wimbledon mixed doubles, recalled a conversation between the pair with Williams opening up about missing top-level tennis.

"She asked if I missed playing," Murray told the BBC. "I was like, 'not at all, to be honest'.

"She said, 'yes, I miss it every single day. I absolutely loved competing and playing. If I could, I'd be back out there again'."

On the prospect of his own return, Murray said: "As much as I would love to, I don't think I'd physically be capable of doing that.

"I haven't missed the sport enough yet to want to get on the court and even hit tennis balls.

"I don't mind hitting the occasional ball if it's required on the practice court, but I don't think the 44-year-old me will be competing."

Sports.title: Spain finally announce World Cup arrival as Yamal, Oyarzabal star in Saudi win
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal were the stars of the show as Spain finally announced their arrival at the 2026 World Cup with a 4-0 thrashing of Saudi Arabia.

The pressure was immense on La Roja to produce not only a win, but a performance after a dismal goalless draw against Cape Verde in their Group H opener on Monday.

It was one of the biggest shocks in the tournament's history - but Spain hit back at any critics with a classic showing of quick passing, attacking football and lots of goals.

Yamal was back in the starting XI after an electric cameo last week and immediately showed why he is one of the best players in the world. He poked home Oyarzabal's low, fizzing cross on a tight angle for his first World Cup goal on his first World Cup start.

He told DAZN after the game that he watched the last tournament in 2022 from his classroom: "Being able to score here with my mum and my family in the stands is a dream come true."

Image: Lamine Yamal celebrates scoring Spain's first goal

Lamine Yamal is only the second player aged 18 or younger to open the scoring in a World Cup match - the other was a 17-year-old Pele for Brazil vs Wales in 1958.

Oyarzabal's quickfire double soon put Spain out of sight - all before the first hydration break in the 25th minute. His first was a scrappy poke home at the back post, before a more intentional finish two minutes later.

He should have completed his hat-trick after collecting a poor back pass from Mohammed Al Owais, but his first-time hit pinged off the top of the crossbar.

Spain's Mikel Oyarzabal is the only player to score two and set up another in the opening 25 minutes of a World Cup match on record (since 1966).

Oyarzabal and Yamal were replaced at half-time, which a smart move from Luis de la Fuente - who celebrated his 65th birthday on Sunday - with more trying tests to come.

While Spain were less intense after the break, they remained dominant, but it was an unfortunate own goal that added the fourth. Marc Cucurella's initial effort from a flicked-on corner was initially well-saved by Al Owais, but the rebound hit Hassan Al Tambakti and into the back of the net.

Image: Spain's Marc Cucurella reacts after Saudi Arabia's Hassan Altambakti scores an own goal, making it 4-0

La Roja thought they had a fifth in added time as Ferran Torres turned home Fabian Ruiz's cross. However, after a lengthy VAR review, the goal was ruled out for offside.

It sends Spain top of Group H ahead of Uruguay's game against Cape Verde at 11pm on Sunday, while Saudi Arabia go bottom.
